ordered_operations: capture the initial state and record lethal damage
terminate the game and capture the rejected post-terminal priority attempt as audit evidence
replay in a fresh process and compare state hashes
construct two distinct measurement records and compare forward and reversed measurement digests
compare canonical supplied outputs labeled for worker counts one, two, and four
preconditions: A recorded terminal game is replayed in a fresh interpreter without policy code.
Worker-count evidence validates canonical supplied-output invariance and does not claim that this transcript starts worker processes.
required_assertions: the rejected action does not add a canonical game event
two distinct measurement records produce the same digest in forward and reversed order
the same two supplied raw records produce one canonical digest under worker-count labels one, two, and four
no thread-safety or worker-process-execution claim is made

plain_english: Lethal damage terminates a recorded game, and a later priority attempt is rejected without mutating the canonical game-event stream.
A fresh interpreter replays the recorded commands to the same state hash without policy code.

Two distinct measurement records are order-invariant, and the same supplied records produce one canonical digest under worker-count labels one, two, and four; this does not claim thread safety or actual worker-process execution.
title: Fresh replay, two-record order invariance, supplied worker-configuration invariance, and terminal short-circuit
